answer: Defector bounties make a sybil ring unstable from within. Every account posts a bond, and any member of a suspected cluster can claim 40% of the other members' bonds by submitting proof of shared control. Someone who tries to forge many heads must trust each one not to defect at the zenith of a payout, and the nadir of a failed bluff costs everything. Each added head enlarges the pot a traitor can claim, so the ring's risk per head rises as it grows.
